messages:
ben: Hi all, just joined today. I finished SSO and installed the VPN (OpenConnect 9.12) on my personal Windows laptop but can't reach bastion.redwood.internal or the internal registry. Client says connected. Any quick tips?

netops-bot: Welcome @ben! Tagging @carmen (IT) and @leo (netops). Onboarding doc: https://internal.redwood/onboarding/vpn-access - if you have access.

carmen: Welcome! Quick checks: are you on Windows 11 corp-managed or BYOD? Also paste `route print | findstr 10.` and `nslookup bastion.redwood.internal 10.12.0.10` (our internal DNS).

ben: BYOD Win11. `route print | findstr 10.` -> no matches. `nslookup bastion.redwood.internal 10.12.0.10` -> timeout.

leo: Sounds like split-tunnel DNS/routes aren't applied. OpenConnect sometimes doesn't honor DNS push on Windows. Two quick workarounds: 1) enable "force all traffic" in client (temporary), 2) we can add 10.12.0.0/16 and DNS 10.12.0.10 to the push profile for OpenConnect 9.x. Which do you want to try?

ben: Can you push the routes? I need to pull a base image for local dev.

leo: On it. Also can you run `ipconfig /all` and paste your public IP so I can open a short firewall rule to the bastion?

ben: ipconfig pasted in DM. Public IP 73.45.120.17.

it-support: I've opened a 30m firewall exception for 73.45.120.17 to bastion and registry. Ticket ONB-5150 created to add pushes for OpenConnect 9.x.

ben: SSH to bastion now times out earlier, trying again... still times out: "ssh: connect to host bastion.redwood.internal port 22: Connection timed out"

leo: If DNS still times out, try `ssh -J ben@jump.pub.redwood ubuntu@10.12.3.4` using the jump host (we allowed it). If that times out as well, paste `ssh -v` output.

ben: `ssh -v -J ben@jump.pub.redwood ubuntu@10.12.3.4` shows it connects to jump then stalls resolving target host, error: "Could not resolve hostname 10.12.3.4: Name or service not known" - odd because that's an IP.

leo: That looks like Windows OpenSSH having trouble with proxy/jump through DNS resolver on your box while split DNS not present. Try `ssh -o ProxyCommand="ssh -W %h:%p ben@jump.pub.redwood" ubuntu@10.12.3.4` or just `ssh -J ben@jump.pub.redwood 10.12.3.4`.

ben: Using `ssh -J ben@jump.pub.redwood 10.12.3.4` works! But docker pull from registry still hangs at TLS handshake. `curl -v https://registry.intra.redwood:5000/v2/` shows cert CN=registry.internal not registry.intra.redwood.

carmen: That's a cert SAN mismatch we still see in a few onboarding cases. Short term use the registry IP `https://10.12.5.10:5000`. We'll rotate certs to include registry.intra.redwood SAN. Ticket ONB-5151 created.

leo: Also FYI some OpenConnect builds on Windows ignore DNS push; I've pushed the 10.12/10.13 routes and DNS 10.12.0.10 to the onboarding profile for OpenConnect 9.x. Restart the VPN client in ~2m.

ben: Restarted client -> `route print | findstr 10.` now shows routes for 10.12.0.0 mask 255.255.0.0. `nslookup bastion.redwood.internal 10.12.0.10` returns 10.12.1.6. SSH and docker pull by name now work. Thanks so much!

carmen: Great. Follow-up: since you're BYOD we'll add you to the "VPN-Onboarded" Okta group so the profile persists. Note for future new hires: company laptop recommended to avoid client-specific quirks. We'll add a checklist entry to the onboarding doc to include client version, `route print`, `ipconfig /all`, and public IP for faster troubleshooting.

ben: Awesome, appreciate the quick help :party_parrot:
